meta.triageRationale: One cohesive story with real design choices (which highlighter to bundle and how, how a diff line is highlighted when each line is a fragment of a file, how token colours follow the VS Code theme, whether fenced code blocks share it) and several build tasks across the diff widget renderer, the shared stylesheet and a vendored asset. It reuses the existing diff sections and the vendored-library pattern, so there is no new subsystem or cross-service contract and it is not an epic.

findings.premise: The reviewer's feedback (click a diff section to open the file at the relevant line) is designed. It is contract 2.2, migration step 4, ac5 and its tests. The non-goal (fenced code blocks in replies sharing the highlighter) is not built.
findings.evidence: Section 2.2 defines the open-code-ref click from the line and from the header path. Section 9 leaves fenced code blocks to a follow-up. The markdown path (render-registry.ts:435, marked.parse into innerHTML) is not touched by any step. [files: vscode-plugin/src/chat/render-registry.ts]

findings.premise: Each diff line today is a div with a number span, a sign span and one text span set as plain text. The number is the old-side number for a removed line and the new-side number otherwise. A '\' line is a note.

So at a removed line newNo is the number the next new-side line takes, which matches the design's rule for line numbers. [files: vscode-plugin/src/chat/render-registry.ts]

summary.prose: Added and removed lines in the chat's diff widget are coloured by syntax, in the language of the changed file, using the editor theme's colours. The page tokenises each side of a diff section with a bundled highlighter, so a comment or string that spans lines stays correct, and a file it does not know, or any failure, shows the plain text it shows today. The change stays inside the page: no new message, no stored data and no change to the CSP. Clicking a line of a diff section, or the file's path in its header, also opens that file in the editor at the relevant line, through the same message and host opener the chat's code-reference links use, so it opens in the same editor group.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Add syntax highlighting to the chat diff widget

api.name: renderRegistryWebviewSource
api.signature: function renderRegistryWebviewSource(): string  // the page script it returns gains: diffTokens(path: string, lines: readonly string[]): Array<Array<{ text: string; cls?: string | undefined }>> | undefined

parameters.name: path
parameters.purpose: the changed file's path, whose extension picks the language

parameters.name: lines
parameters.purpose: the section's diff lines with their ' ', '+', '-' or '\' prefix

returns.type: Array<Array<{ text: string; cls?: string | undefined }>> | undefined
returns.meaning: for each diff line, its text as runs of plain text and classed tokens; undefined when the language is unknown or tokenising failed, and the widget then writes the line as plain text, as today. Token classes map to existing :root names in chat-panel.ts, which approximate the editor's token colours and do not reproduce them: keyword to --magenta, string to --accent, number to --amber, function and title to --user, type and built-in to --accent2, comment to --muted, and meta, attribute and tag to --link (each of those is already a VS Code theme variable)

errors.condition: an unknown extension, a missing highlighter or any throw while tokenising returns undefined and is never shown as an error

preconditions: the highlighter source has been evaluated in the page before the rows are rendered
postconditions: each line's text span holds only text nodes and class-named spans built by DOM construction, never assigned markup
the sign, the line number and the add/del background are unchanged
the old side (context and removed lines) and the new side (context and added lines) are tokenised separately, so a removed line is never read as part of the added text

the highlighter's output is turned into runs by a string scanner over its restricted markup (span open with a class, span close, and the five entities & < > " '); nested spans are flattened so the innermost class wins, a span that crosses a newline continues on the next line's runs, and any other tag or entity makes the scanner return undefined; a span whose class has no hljs- prefix (a sub-language wrapper) is read as classless text, not as a reason to reject

dataModelChanges.details: No field changes. The section's lines are tokenised in the page from the existing path and lines; nothing is added to the row message or the stored transcript, so rows already stored are highlighted the same way as new ones. The page also gains a bundled highlighter string and a small extension-to-language map, and the widget's stylesheet gains token classes whose colours come from VS Code theme variables. Token colours are not new --vscode-* names: the token rules in the widget's style (RENDER_REGISTRY_STYLE) name only the existing :root layer in chat-panel.ts, so the tests that forbid a --vscode- name in the widget rules and keep the exhaustive list of referenced theme variables stay valid. The added selectors are added to the inline added-selector list in chat-theme.test.ts; chat-theme-before.json is the frozen before-fixture and is not edited. diff-sections.ts is read, not changed: the section's path and lines are the input. The new generated highlighter module is produced by vscode-plugin/gen-webview-libs.mjs. The highlighter goes into its own generated module (webview-hljs.ts), imported only by chat-panel.ts; webview-marked.ts is not changed, and docs-review-panel.ts, which also inlines the marked string, is unchanged and gets no highlighter, so its single-script test is untouched. Existing tests that read a diff line's text span are affected differently by suite. chat-shell.test.ts runs the whole page script over the shared fake DOM, and its diff rows use a path in the language map, so its text-span assertions would read an empty textContent once the span is built from children: the shared fake's textContent getter is made to join the text of its children when it has any, as the real DOM does, and createTextNode is wired into that suite's document stub; the assertions are unchanged. render-registry.test.ts has its own local fake node and document, sets no highlighter global, so its existing diff assertions stay on the plain-text path and are unchanged; the new tokenising unit tests use the shared fake DOM with a highlighter global injected. Other suites that use the shared fake are re-run to confirm the join changes none of them. A diff line element also gains two data attributes, its path and its new-side line, written while the row is built; a delegated click handler in the registry posts the existing open-code-ref message through the registry's link-open sink. The row message and stored rows are still unchanged.

errorCases.scenario: The highlighter throws or is missing in the page
errorCases.detection: diffTokens wraps the whole tokenising call in try/catch and checks that the highlighter global is defined before using it
errorCases.response: diffTokens returns undefined and the widget writes every line as plain text, as today

errorCases.scenario: The file's extension has no language in the map
errorCases.detection: The extension-to-language lookup finds no entry (or the language is not in the bundled subset)
errorCases.response: diffTokens returns undefined; no guessing from the content

errorCases.scenario: The highlighter returns markup that is not the expected spans and text
errorCases.detection: The string scanner over the highlighter's output accepts only a span open with a class attribute, a span close and the five entities, and returns undefined at anything else
errorCases.response: The whole section falls back to plain text

errorCases.scenario: A section is large (up to the saved line limit) and tokenising is slow
errorCases.detection: The page tokenises each side only when its widget row is built, and a section is at most the saved line limit
errorCases.response: The row is built once and not re-tokenised when the widget is opened or closed
errorCases.userImpact: A short delay when a large diff first appears

errorCases.scenario: The bundled highlighter text contains <script or </script (for example the HTML grammar's own regex)
errorCases.detection: The generator scans the bundled string and escapes every '<' that starts '<script' or '</script' as \x3c, and the build fails if the check still finds one
errorCases.response: The module cannot be emitted with a literal script tag in it, so the shell's single-script check and the browser's inline script both stay valid
errorCases.userImpact: None at run time; a developer sees the failed generation

errorCases.scenario: A clicked section's file cannot be opened (a deleted file, or the chat's folder is not the workspace folder the host resolves from)
errorCases.detection: The host's link opener refuses the path (it is missing, or does not resolve inside the workspace folder) and logs
errorCases.response: Nothing opens and the widget does not change

migration.stateBefore: Each diff line in the widget is a div holding a line-number span, a sign span and one text span set from the line as plain text, with add and del backgrounds; no highlighter is bundled and the page's only library is marked, evaluated from a generated string inside the one nonce'd script (render-registry.ts, webview-marked.ts and chat-panel.ts, from the s1 bundles).
migration.stateAfter: The page also evaluates a generated highlighter string with a fixed language subset. For each diff section the widget tokenises the old side and the new side separately, maps the tokens back to their lines and builds each line's text span from text nodes and class-named spans. Token classes take their colours from VS Code theme variables. An unknown language or any failure leaves the plain text. The row message, stored rows and CSP are unchanged.

migrationSteps.action: Add the highlighter as its own generated webview module (webview-hljs.ts) produced by gen-webview-libs.mjs, bundling highlight.js core and the language subset into one self-contained string (built with esbuild, already a devDependency), escaping any script tag text in it, and record the added size; webview-marked.ts is not touched

Add the extension-to-language map and the tokenising of each section side, with the string scanner that turns the highlighter's output into per-line runs and the plain-text fallback, to the widget's renderer in the page script

Evaluate the highlighter string in the chat shell next to marked (chat-panel.ts only; the review pane's page is unchanged), and add the token class rules, using only the existing :root colour names, to the widget's stylesheet, adding the new selectors to the inline list in chat-theme.test.ts in the same commit

Write each diff line's path and new-side line as data attributes when the row is built, add the delegated click handler that posts the existing open-code-ref message, and make the header's path open the file while the rest of the header still toggles the widget

migration.backwardCompat: Additive and page-only: no message, stored data or CSP change, and stored diff rows are highlighted the same way as new ones. A page that cannot run the highlighter shows the plain diff it shows today.

alternativesConsidered.name: Bundle highlight.js core with a language subset, tokenise each side of a section
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A bundled highlight.js subset tokenises each side of a diff section; token classes take the theme's colours.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Generate a webview string for highlight.js core plus a fixed set of common languages (selected by file extension through a small extension-to-language map), exactly as marked is bundled, and evaluate it in the one nonce'd script. For a section, rebuild the old side (context and removed lines) and the new side (context and added lines) as two texts and tokenise each, so a comment or string that spans lines is carried across them; then turn the result into per-line runs with a string scanner over its restricted span markup and build each line's text span from text nodes and class-named spans, never inline colours or assigned markup. Token classes map to theme variables in the widget's rules. An unknown extension, a missing library or a thrown error leaves the plain text.
pros: A maintained tokeniser with real grammars for many languages
Follows the existing vendored-library pattern, no CDN and no CSP change
Tokenising each side keeps multi-line comments and strings correct
Fenced code blocks in replies can reuse it later
Reuses the open-code-ref message and the host opener, so clicking a diff line shares the links' safety checks and editor placement
cons: Adds a sizeable generated asset to the one inline script, so shell size grows
highlight.js emits HTML text, so it is read by a string scanner and never assigned as markup
Only the languages in the subset are highlighted

alternativesConsidered.name: A small hand-written tokeniser in the page
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A compact in-house tokeniser covers the common languages with no new dependency.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Write a compact tokeniser of our own for the families the repo mostly changes (TypeScript and JavaScript, JSON, Python, shell, Markdown, YAML, CSS, HTML): comments, strings, numbers and keywords from short per-language lists. It runs per section side like a1 and builds token spans by DOM construction with textContent, so it never assigns markup. The language comes from a small extension map and anything else stays plain.
pros: No new dependency and a small asset
Built by DOM construction with textContent, so no markup is ever assigned
Fully under our control and tested
cons: Less accurate than real grammars (regex literals, template nesting, heredocs)
Every new language is more code for us to maintain
Likely to look wrong at the edges and draw bug reports
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: No dependency and no markup, but it trades accuracy for size, and accuracy is the project's first principle; its edge cases would keep producing wrong colours.

alternativesConsidered.name: Tokenise in the extension host with a TextMate grammar engine
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The host tokenises with TextMate grammars and sends token lists to the page.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Do the tokenising in the extension host with a TextMate engine and grammars, and send the tokens with each diff row, so the page only paints spans. The row message gains a per-line token list.
pros: The same grammar family VS Code uses, so the most accurate result
cons: Adds a heavy native or WASM dependency to the extension and a larger package
Changes the row message and the stored transcript rows, so old rows stay unhighlighted
More moving parts and a slower first render
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: The most accurate result, but a heavy dependency, a changed row message and old rows left unhighlighted make it disproportionate for a colouring feature.

openQuestions: The contract entry names the existing symbol renderRegistryWebviewSource while describing the new page function diffTokens (a schema workaround); diffTokens, the highlighter string and the language map are new.
The Story has no acceptance criteria; ac1-ac4 were derived from its stated needs.
Whether fenced code blocks in assistant replies share the highlighter is left out of this Story and is a candidate follow-up.

Which languages the bundled subset holds, and the size it adds to the one inline script, are settled and recorded at build; the generator builds the core plus subset with esbuild, a different step from marked's prebuilt-file copy.

The section's path is relative to the folder the diff ran in, and the host resolves a clicked path from the first workspace folder; if the chat's folder is not that workspace folder, the click is refused and logged. Carrying the folder with the click is left for a follow-up.
